No adjustment for post-manipulation brood size (a mediator/collider); year included as environmental confounder since unmanipulated broods were not matched to manipulated ones. Orientation: larger net_rearing_manipulation = more siblings = more competition, i.e., as_declared; negative coefficient indicates more competition reduces nestling growth.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (net number of chicks added to the rearing brood via experimental cross-fostering, in signed chicks: negative = reduction, 0 = unmanipulated, positive = enlargement)

rows.note: Primary analysis: linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML fit) of day_14_weight on net_rearing_manipulation (net chicks added to the rearing brood via cross-fostering; positive = enlarged = MORE sibling competition), with random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID), and fixed effects for hatch_year (factor), chick molecular sex as a 3-level factor including the 1,094 '.'-unknown chicks as their own level (not dropped, to avoid sample distortion), and rearing-nest hatching date (rear_nest_OH, centered). Exclusions: 85 chicks with missing ('.') net_rearing_manipulation dropped; day-14 weight complete. Focal slope = -0.180 g per additional sibling, model-based SE 0.016, z = -11.58. Design-based check with identical fixed effects via OLS and cluster-robust SE clustered by rearing nest: slope -0.174, SE 0.0152, t = -11.41, 95% CI [-0.204, -0.144]; reported SE 0.0155 is the average of the model-based (0.0155) and cluster-robust (0.0152) SEs, which are virtually identical. Focal estimate in native scale: grams of day-14 mass per one additional sibling (test statistic: z = -11.58 for mixed model; t = -11.41 cluster-robust with G-1 = 438 design df). n = 3,635 chicks (observation unit = chick), 439 rearing-nest clusters, mean 8.3 chicks/nest. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment (2001-2003 Wytham Wood blue tits) with treatment assigned at the brood level. No post-treatment covariates (tarsus, day-14 brood size) adjusted for. Each extra sibling reduces day-14 mass by ~0.18 g (~1.7% of mean mass 10.28 g), indicating strong sibling-competition effects on nestling growth.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood by the cross-fostering manipulation; positive = enlarged brood = more sibling competition; includes unmanipulated broods at 0)

rows.note: OLS of day_14_weight (g) on net_rearing_manipulation (net chicks added to rearing brood via cross-fostering; continuous, negative=reduced, positive=enlarged, 0=unmanipulated), adjusting for hatch_year (factor), rearing-nest hatch date (rear_nest_OH), and rearing-nest starting brood size (rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing). Cluster-robust SEs clustered on rear_nest_breed_ID (396 rearing nests). Fitted n = 3,315 chicks (complete cases on outcome, manipulation, covariates); 405 rows dropped for missing net_rearing_manipulation (85) or starting brood size (387); chick sex excluded as covariate because 1,094 unknown molecular sexes would induce sample loss (sensitivity sex-adjusted fit on n=2,367 gave -0.067 g, SE 0.028 — concordant). Observation unit: chick; design: between-nest brood-size manipulation, chicks clustered in rearing nests. Focal estimate: -0.093 g day-14 mass per net chick added; t = -3.82 (cluster-robust), model residual df = 3,309; 95% CI [-0.141, -0.045]. More siblings = more competition, reducing nestling growth.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (net chicks added to the rearing brood by cross-fostering, continuous, signed; positive = enlarged brood, negative = reduced brood, 0 = unmanipulated)

rows.note: Model: OLS, day_14_weight (g) ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size + C(hatch_year) + rear_nest_OH + C(sex3), with cluster-robust SEs clustered on rear_nest_breed_ID (statsmodels cov_type="cluster"). n = 3,720 chicks (full dataset; no rows excluded — outcome, exposure, year, and rear-nest hatch date are complete). chick_sex_molec missing for 1,094 chicks was kept as its own covariate level ("unknown") instead of listwise deletion, preserving the declared frame; a sensitivity fit dropping those rows gives b = -0.115 (SE 0.015), same conclusion. Focal estimate: coefficient on d14_rear_nest_brood_size = -0.0932 g per additional chick in the day-14 rearing brood, SE 0.0134, t = -6.94, inferential df = 451 (452 rearing-nest clusters - 1). Observation unit = chick. Design: chick-level cross-sectional regression over the experimental cross-fostering brood-manipulation gradient (167 enlarged, 165 reduced, 120 unmanipulated rearing broods); larger brood = more sibling competition, so the negative sign indicates each additional nestmate reduces day-14 mass by ~0.09 g, controlling for year, within-season hatch date, and sex. Orientation: larger values of the focal predictor correspond to MORE sibling competition (as_declared). Native scale: grams of day-14 mass per one additional chick.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (realized number of chicks in the rearing brood at day 14; coefficient = grams of day-14 mass per one additional sibling/nestmate)

rows.note: Focal model: linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML) of day_14_weight (g) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + hatch_year + chick_sex_molec (3 levels incl. 1094 unknown) + rear_nest_CS + rear_nest_OH, with a random intercept per rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Focal estimate: -0.183 g of day-14 mass per net chick added to the rearing brood (SE 0.0154, t = -11.92, residual df ~3586, fitted n = 3,594 chicks in 434 rearing broods; observation unit = individual chick; design = nest-level brood-size manipulation via cross-fostering). Data handling: '.' recoded to missing; rear_nest_trt decoding verified empirically (5=enlarged/167 nests, 6=reduced/165, 7=unmanipulated/120); net_rearing_manipulation verified as nest-level (within-nest sd=0) and equal to rear_Cs_in - rear_Cs_out. Exclusions: 85 chicks whose entire nests lack a manipulation value (nest-level missing assignment, not imputable) and 41 chicks in nests without rear_nest_CS; kept all rows with complete outcomes and covariates otherwise. Random intercept variance 0.604 g^2; residual 0.486 g^2. Caveat: manipulated broods were matched to each other but not to unmanipulated controls, so the linear manipulation term partially relies on cross-design comparability.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: net number of chicks added to the rearing brood by the experimental brood-size manipulation (positive = enlarged = more sibling competition, negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated), entered as a continuous linear term

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, ML fit, converged) of day-14 weight (g) on net_rearing_manipulation (continuous: net chicks added at cross-fostering, negative for reductions, 0 for unmanipulated), with fixed covariates rear_nest_CS (rearing-nest clutch size, pre-manipulation baseline) and hatch year factor (2001/2002/2003), and a random intercept per rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Exclusions: 85 chicks with missing net_rearing_manipulation (53 in enlarged, 32 in reduced manipulated broods — cannot be recoded to 0, so dropped) and 41 chicks missing rear_nest_CS; 1,094 chicks with unknown molecular sex retained (sex omitted from model to preserve sample). Fitted n = 3,594 chicks in 434 rearing broods. Focal estimate: -0.182 g per additional sibling (SE 0.0156, z = -11.62, p < 0.001, 95% CI [-0.212, -0.151]). Observation unit: chick; design: cluster-randomized-style brood-size manipulation with chick-level outcomes clustered within rearing nests (mean 8.3 chicks/brood). Inferential df: MixedLM reports a z statistic; 434 rearing broods is the conservative cluster-level df for the treatment effect. rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing was NOT adjusted for because it is post-treatment (brood size after manipulation, r = 0.77 with the manipulation). Positive manipulation values = more siblings = more competition, so orientation is as_declared; the negative sign means more sibling competition reduces nestling mass, consistent with the estimand.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (continuous, in chicks added by brood manipulation: -4 to +4, 0 = unmanipulated; per-1-chick contrast in day-14 grams)

rows.note: Chick-level OLS of day-14 weight (g) on signed net_rearing_manipulation (chicks added to rearing brood; positive=enlarged, negative=reduced), with hatch_year fixed effects, standard errors clustered by rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Frame: only experimentally manipulated broods (rear_nest_trt 5 or 6); 85 chicks with missing manipulation ('.') and the 919 unmanipulated-brood chicks excluded. Fitted n = 2,716 chicks in 319 rearing nests. Focal coefficient: -0.1670 g (SE 0.0145), t = -11.525 (cluster-robust), p ≈ 5e-30; cluster-count-consistent df ≈ 315 (319 nests − 4 params); statsmodels-reported residual df = 2712. Observation unit: chick, nested within rearing brood; design: matched-pair cross-fostering brood-size manipulation. Secondary outcome day-14 tarsus shows same direction: -0.0626 mm/chick (SE 0.0075, t = -8.31). Interpretation: each additional sibling reduces day-14 mass by ~0.17 g (~1.6% of mean mass ~10.3 g). Predictor construction: numeric net_rearing_manipulation entered as a single signed continuous term (per-net-chick linear contrast).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (net number of chicks added to the rearing brood via cross-fostering; signed continuous, +4 to -4)

rows.note: Chick-level OLS: day_14_weight ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size + C(sex, 3 levels incl. unknown) + C(hatch_year) + rear_nest_OH, all 3,720 chicks (no exclusions; sex '.' coded as its own category). Cluster-robust SEs (small-sample corrected) clustered on rear_nest_breed_ID (452 clusters). Focal slope = -0.0932 g day-14 mass per additional sibling in the rearing brood (SE 0.0134, t = -6.94, cluster df = 451, 95% CI [-0.120, -0.067]). Observation unit: chick; design: brood-size-manipulation experiment, chicks cross-fostered between enlarged/reduced/unmanipulated rearing nests. Native scale: grams per sibling. Larger brood size = more competition = less growth.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size: day-14 brood size of the rearing nest (number of siblings cohabiting), as a continuous predictor in a linear model for day-14 mass

rows.note: Focal estimate: effect of net rearing brood-size manipulation (net_rearing_manipulation, continuous, −4 to +4 chicks added; experimentally cross-fostered brood enlargements/reductions plus unmanipulated broods at 0) on day-14 nestling mass (grams) in blue tits, Wytham Wood 2001–2003. Model: ML linear mixed model day_14_weight ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year), random intercept for rearing nest (rear_nest_breed_ID). Sample: 3,635 chicks with non-missing day-14 weight and net manipulation (85 of 3,720 excluded for missing net_rearing_manipulation), 439 rearing nests, unit of observation = individual chick. Focal coefficient = −0.1807 g per net additional sibling (SE 0.0157, t = −11.48, df_resid = 3631, p < 0.001). Nest-level clustering was substantial (nest variance 0.64 vs residual 0.53); a nest-clustered GEE with exchangeable working correlation corroborates the result (estimate −0.1807, robust SE 0.0152). Interpretation: each experimentally added sibling reduced day-14 mass by ~0.18 g (~1.8% of the 10.29 g mean), indicating a strong negative effect of sibling competition on nestling growth.
rows.predictor: Coefficient on net_rearing_manipulation (net number of chicks added to the rearing brood by the cross-fostering manipulation, continuous −4 to +4, unmanipulated = 0), signed as entered in the model

rows.note: Primary analysis: OLS of chick day-14 weight (grams) on net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to the rearing brood via cross-fostering: negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated, positive = enlarged; range −4 to +4), adjusted for hatch_year (categorical), rear_nest_OH (rearing-nest hatching date), and rear_nest_CS (rearing-nest clutch size, included because manipulation magnitude scales with original brood size and unmanipulated broods were not matched). Unit of observation: individual chick. Sample: 3,594 chicks from 434 rearing nests, 2001–2003 (started from all 3,720 measured chicks; excluded 85 with missing net_rearing_manipulation and 41 with missing rear_nest_CS). Inference: cluster-robust (sandwich) SEs clustered on rear_nest_breed_ID (452 clusters in full data; 434 in fitted sample), since competition exposure is applied at the rearing-brood level. Focal estimate: −0.1775 g of day-14 mass per net sibling added; cluster-robust SE = 0.0150; t(≈433 effective df, z-normal reference) = −11.81, p ≈ 3.3e−32; 95% CI [−0.207, −0.148]. More competition reduces nestling growth. Robustness: restricted to manipulated broods only (randomized/matched subset, n = 2,709) gives −0.170 (SE 0.0145); nest-level analysis of brood-mean mass (n = 435 nests, HC1 SEs) gives −0.186 (SE 0.0152); a quadratic term is small (−0.032, p < 0.0001) indicating a weakly accelerating effect at extreme manipulations, but the linear per-chick contrast dominates. Residuals are mildly left-skewed (skew −0.80), unlikely to matter at t ≈ −11.8. Outcome analyzed on its native gram scale; no effect-size conversion.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood by the cross-fostering brood-size manipulation (one numeric variable, per-chick, from the experimental enlargement/reduction of rearing broods; coefficient = change in day-14 mass in grams per additional sibling)

rows.note: Focal model: chick-level linear regression of day-14 mass on signed net_rearing_manipulation, using matched-pair fixed effects, with cluster-robust standard errors clustered by matched pair. Unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not part of the matched-pair randomization. Matched pairs were reconstructed from the full cross-foster graph, giving 136 complete enlarged/reduced pairs and 2,327 chicks. Test statistic: t = -10.9421 with 135 df. Observation unit: chick. Design: matched-pair brood-size manipulation with within-pair fixed-effects contrast.
rows.predictor: signed net_rearing_manipulation (number of chicks added to the rearing brood; negative = reduced, positive = enlarged)

rows.note: Focal analysis: OLS of day-14 mass (g) on d14_rear_nest_brood_size (realized number of nestmates in the rearing nest at day 14), adjusting for breeding-season year (factors, 2001–2003) and rearing-nest hatch date (linear), with cluster-robust standard errors clustered on rearing nest (452 clusters). Full sample: all 3,720 chicks (outcome and focal predictor complete; '.' coded as NaN). Focal estimate: b = −0.0934 g per additional nestmate, SE = 0.0136, t = −6.861 (cluster-robust), p ≈ 7e-12, residual df = 3716, 8 model parameters. Interpretation: each additional sibling reduces day-14 mass by ~0.093 g (95% CI ≈ −0.120 to −0.067); an enlargement of ~4 chicks implies ~0.37 g loss (~3.6% of mean mass 10.28 g). Linearity check: quadratic brood-size term coef −0.0056, p = 0.104 — no clear rejection of linearity. Chick sex excluded from the primary model because molecular sex is missing for 1,094 chicks (30%); a complete-case model adjusting for sex gives b = −0.1153, SE = 0.0154, t = −7.505 (n = 2,626), consistent with the primary estimate. An earlier full-sample specification using a missing-sex indicator produced distorted sex coefficients (recoding artifact) and was discarded. Observation unit: chick; design: chick-level cross-section from the Wytham Wood brood-size manipulation experiment (2001–2003), 452 rearing nests. The manipulation provides exogenous variation in rearing brood size; realized day-14 brood size is the competition intensity actually experienced (early mortality being partly a consequence of competition). No chicks excluded.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size — the number of nestmates in the chick's rearing nest at day 14 (realized sibling-competition intensity), entered as a single signed numeric quantity: grams of day-14 mass per additional nestmate. Larger values = more siblings competing.
